To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
selenium intake and plasma levels are inversely related to risk of prostate cancer and, more specifically, to risk of high-grade prostate cancer.
the selenium status of men with prostate cancer is associated with the stage of the disease at diagnosis and with PSA levels.

selenium supplementation reduces the incidence of prostate cancer in men with a history of the disease and that selenium supplementation reduces prostate cancer mortality in men with prostate cancer who have not yet metastasized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of selenium in the prevention of human cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of selenium in prostate carcinogenesis.
the effects of the trace element selenium on the initiation and promotion of carcinogenesis in the rat ventral prostate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence from epidemiology, preclinical studies, and randomized prevention trials indicates that selenium is a promising chemopreventive agent for prostate cancer.
selenium is an essential micronutrient that, in the context of a balanced diet, is required for the maintenance of health.
selenium is an important nutrient in the prevention of cancer, and that selenium may be an important nutrient in prostate cancer prevention.

the results of the NPC trial are not inconsistent with the results of the observational study by Li et al. (1,3) and the other observational studies.
the effects of selenium are not due to a single mechanism but to the interplay of several mechanisms, including effects on the cell cycle, on the immune system, and on oxidative stress.
selenium is a cancer-preventive agent.
